newsitem.title: USA: US Sept consumer confidence 111.8 vs revised 112.0. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: US Sept consumer confidence 111.8 vs revised 112.0. [CORRECTED 15:50 GMT]

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence slipped lightly to 111.8 in September from a revised reading of 112.0 in August, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.

The expectations component of the September (corrects from August) index rose to 100.4 from a revised 100.3 in the previous month, and the current conditions component fell to 129.0 versus a revised reading of 129.5 in August.
The survey showed consumers are "quite optimistic about the next six months," the Conference Board said. "With consumers in high spirits, the outlook for holiday spending appears to be bright."

In addition to posting the national measures, the survey showed regional confidence has improved dramatically in New England over the past three months, rising 24 percent. Confidence levels there had been "in the doldrums since early 1990," the Conference Board said.

The East South Central region -- including Kentucky, Tennessee, Alabama and Mississippi -- was the only area to report a decline in confidence over the past three months, dropping about 1.0 percent, the Board said.
